summary: The Branco Weiss Fellowship 2027 call is open now. The registration portal is live, and applications close on 15 January 2027 at 5 p.m. CET. Shortlisting happens in May 2027, Zoom interviews and final decisions on 7–9 June 2027, and fellowships start between 1 October and 31 December 2027. Carlos does NOT appear eligible for this round: applicants must officially hold the PhD (defence passed) by 15 January 2027, and his PhD is expected in March 2027. He would be eligible for the following call. Based on this cycle, its deadline would be around mid-January 2028 (estimated, not announced). The project must also clearly depart from mainstream research in its field and engage with social, cultural, political or economic issues beyond the discipline. A mainstream Majorana or hybrid-nanowire theory proposal would probably not be funded.
eligibility: Applicants must hold the PhD by the deadline (15 Jan 2027 for this round) and have obtained it no more than 5 years before that date. Only parental leave or illness/accident leave can extend this, by up to 1 year in total, and the confirmation must be emailed before applying. Applicants must not hold or have held a faculty-equivalent or independent PI position. Any field and any nationality can apply. There is no mobility or residence rule, but applicants must be able to travel to the Greater Zurich Area for the annual symposium in person. The project must be unconventional and outside the mainstream, show society engagement, and come with an outstanding track record. The applicant chooses any host institution worldwide. The chosen mentor or host may support only one applicant per round. Unsuccessful applicants may reapply.
duration: Up to 5 years: a 2.5-year pioneer phase, a review with a site visit before the end of year 2, then a 2.5-year exploitation phase. The fellowship continues if the fellow takes up a faculty position after year 1.
salary: Up to CHF 600,000 over up to 5 years. It covers legitimate research costs, such as the fellow's salary, equipment, travel, consumables and personnel.

title: SNSF Ambizione
relevance_reason: Your listed PIs in eligible host countries are excluded by the rules (see notes).
summary: The SNSF Ambizione 2026 call was the last one. It opened on 3 August 2026 and closed on 3 November 2026 at 17:00 CET, so it has been closed since 6 days before today (2026-11-09). There will be no Ambizione call in 2027. The SNSF is replacing Ambizione and Postdoc.Mobility with a new combined postdoctoral scheme, which it says will launch in 2028. Details on the 2027 transition were expected by the end of 2026, so the '2028' opening is an estimate and no deadline has been announced. Carlos is not eligible for Ambizione and would not have been eligible for the 2026 call. His PhD is only expected in March 2027, and the scheme required at least 12 months of research after the PhD by the deadline. It also requires a Swiss link: Swiss nationality, a Swiss master's or PhD, or at least 12 months of research at a Swiss institution after the doctorate. He is Spanish, trained in Spain, and has no Swiss research stay. He should watch for the 2028 successor scheme, whose eligibility rules are not yet published. A Swiss link may well apply again, which a postdoc in Switzerland, for example in Titus Neupert's group in Zurich, could provide.
eligibility: 2026 call (final): applicants needed a PhD and had to apply no more than 4 years after the PhD defence (up to 9 years after the medical exam for MDs with at least 3 years of clinical work). Time-window extensions were possible for reasons in Clause 1.11 of the regulations. They needed at least 12 months of research after the PhD by the deadline, with no exceptions. A Swiss link was mandatory: Swiss nationality, a Swiss degree (master's, doctorate, medical diploma or FMH title), or at least 12 months of research at a Swiss institution between the doctorate and the deadline. A statement of mobility justifying the choice of host and describing past and planned mobility was required and counted in the evaluation. Rejected applicants could resubmit once, and Ambizione 2026 applicants cannot apply for SNSF Starting Grants 2027. Carlos does not meet these rules: his PhD is expected in March 2027 and he has no Swiss link.
duration: Up to 4 years. Part-time work at a minimum of 0.8 FTE is possible for family care reasons. Projects selected in the 2026 call start between 1 September 2027 and 1 September 2028.
salary: The grant pays the grantee's own salary for up to 4 years plus project funds of up to about CHF 250,000. The CHF 250,000 figure comes from USI's summary of the call, not the SNSF page itself. Project funds can cover a research stay abroad of up to 1 year, conferences, and technicians or scientific collaborators, but not PhD students or postdocs. An "Ambizione project grant" variant covers project funds only.

relevance_reason: Could be hosted by Fabian Hassler, Piet Brouwer, Felix von Oppen from your PI list.
summary: There are no call windows. The DFG Walter Benjamin Programme takes proposals at any time through the elan portal, and a decision takes about 6 months on average. It funds early-career postdocs to carry out their own project, usually for up to two years. In Germany you hold a postdoc position at the host, normally paid at 100%, plus €250 a month for project, travel and publication costs. Abroad you get a fellowship instead (basic amount plus allowances). Carlos appears eligible for the German position, for example with Brouwer or von Oppen at FU Berlin or Hassler at RWTH Aachen: that track has no nationality or prior-Germany-work rules, and he would be changing institution from ICMM-CSIC. He can submit once his dissertation has been handed in (expected around early 2027, with proof of submission and a supervisor statement), but funding only starts after the doctorate is completed. That makes a start around late 2027 realistic. He is not eligible for the abroad fellowship (for example a stay in Copenhagen), because he has not been integrated into the German research system.
eligibility: For postdocs in the early phase after the doctorate (EU 'recognised researcher', R2). DFG sets no fixed number of years since the PhD, and parental leave is taken into account. You can submit once the dissertation has been handed in, but funding starts only after the doctorate is completed. You must generally change institution (not the PhD institution or current one, except with special justification). You must not have worked more than one year at the chosen host when you submit. German position: no nationality or prior-Germany restrictions. Abroad fellowship: you need to have worked at least 3 continuous years in Germany just before the proposal, or have done most of your schooling and higher education in Germany with no more than 3 years abroad for research since the PhD. Carlos does not meet these. The host cannot be for-profit and must allow open publication.
duration: As a rule up to 24 months. The German position and the abroad fellowship modules can be combined. In France, fellowships are limited to 12 months unless you move to a second French institution.
salary: German position: a postdoc post ('postdoctoral researcher and comparable'), usually at 100%, plus €250 a month for direct project, travel and publication costs. The exact pay scale is not stated. Non-university institutes (Max Planck, Helmholtz, Fraunhofer) must guarantee 45% of the position's funding. Abroad fellowship: a monthly basic amount plus foreign, cost-of-living and travel allowances and benefits for children, paid directly to the fellow.

summary: No call is open today (2026-11-04). The 2026 call (HORIZON-MSCA-2026-PF-01) ran from 9 April to 9 September 2026, with results due around February 2027. The next call, HORIZON-MSCA-2027-PF-01-01, is listed as forthcoming on the EU Funding & Tenders Portal and the MSCA site: planned opening 7 April 2027, deadline 8 September 2027 at 17:00 Brussels time. Some sources still mark these dates as provisional, so check the portal before relying on them. European Fellowships last 12–24 months at a host in an EU Member State or Horizon Europe Associated Country. They pay the researcher living, mobility and, where applicable, family allowances, and pay the host research, training, networking, management and indirect costs. The host PI/organisation writes the proposal with the fellow, submits it, and if funded employs and supervises the fellow. Carlos appears eligible for the 2027 call. His PhD (expected March 2027) would be awarded before the September 2027 deadline, he is well within the 8-year limit, and he has lived only in Spain. That means any host outside Spain (for example Denmark, Germany, the Netherlands, Italy, Sweden or Switzerland) meets the mobility rule. A Spanish host would not. Because his 2025 Copenhagen visit was short, Denmark should still be fine as a host. As an EU national he could also apply for a Global Fellowship to the US or Canada, which adds a mandatory 12-month return phase in Europe. Host institutions often set internal deadlines between April and July, so he should contact host PIs early in 2027.
eligibility: Any nationality (European Fellowships). You need a PhD by the call deadline; a defended thesis counts even before the degree is formally awarded. You can have at most 8 years of research experience after the PhD; career breaks, work outside research, parental leave and long sick leave are not counted. Mobility rule: in the 36 months before the deadline, you must not have lived or had your main activity (work, studies) in the host country for more than 12 months. From 2026, a proposal that scored below 80% the year before cannot be resubmitted with the same host and researcher. Global Fellowships are open only to EU nationals or long-term residents.

summary: The Junior Leader Incoming 2027 call opened on 1 July 2026 and closed on 23 September 2026 at 14:00 Spanish time. The foundation's Spanish page now marks it 'Cerrada' (closed). Shortlisting is due 12 January 2027, interviews 16–17 February 2027 and results 10 March 2027. Fellows start between 1 May and 31 December 2027. Dates for the next call (Incoming 2028) have not been announced. Based on past cycles, it should open around July 2027 and close in late September or early October 2027. The fellowship lasts up to 3 years and is worth up to €320,100 in total. That covers employment costs of up to €64,000 a year (minimum gross salary €47,000 a year) and €38,500 a year for research costs, plus family and mobility allowances. Carlos is NOT currently eligible, for two reasons. (1) His PhD is expected in March 2027, but the PhD must be at least 2 years old at the deadline, so the earliest call he could apply to is the one with a deadline around September 2029. (2) He has lived in Spain all his life, so he fails the Incoming mobility rule for Spanish hosts: no more than 12 months of residence or main activity in Spain in the 3 years before the deadline. He could become eligible for a Spanish host, such as a Severo Ochoa or María de Maeztu centre, after about 2 or more years of postdoc work abroad. Alternatively, he could apply to a host in Portugal, because the mobility rule there is about time spent in Portugal, which he would meet once the PhD-age rule is satisfied. The sister 'Retaining' modality requires at least 12 months in Spain plus at least 6 months of research abroad, and has the same rule that the PhD must be 2–7 years old.
